## Tables {#tables}

43 tables. Click a table name to open its fields.

<div class="dd-static">
<table id="dt-index" class="table table-sm table-striped table-hover data-dictionary-table dd-layout-index">
<thead>
<tr>
<th scope="col" data-dd-key="table" data-dd-mono="true" data-dd-identifier="true" data-dd-groupable="true" data-dd-compact="true" data-dd-filter="input" data-dd-links="table" data-dd-width="200">Table</th>
<th scope="col" data-dd-key="category" data-dd-groupable="true" data-dd-filter="list" data-dd-width="140">Category</th>
<th scope="col" data-dd-key="fields" data-dd-numeric="true" data-dd-compact="true" data-dd-align="right" data-dd-width="90">Fields</th>
<th scope="col" data-dd-key="description" data-dd-clamp="true" data-dd-filter="input" data-dd-min-width="320" data-dd-grow="5">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td class="dd-mono"><a href="#care_site">CARE_SITE</a></td>
<td>Core CDM</td>
<td class="dd-align-right">6</td>
<td>The CARE_SITE table contains a list of uniquely identified institutional (physical or organizational) units where healthcare delivery is practiced (offices, wards, hospitals, clinics, etc.). For Stanford University, this includes a range of care sites from inpatient hospital facilities to outpatient clinics and specialized centers such as immunization and campus-specific health services.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="dd-mono"><a href="#cdm_source">CDM_SOURCE</a></td>
<td>Core CDM</td>
<td class="dd-align-right">11</td>
<td>The CDM_SOURCE table provides information about the source data and the process used to transform the data into the OMOP Common Data Model.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="dd-mono"><a href="#cohort">COHORT</a></td>
<td>Core CDM</td>
<td class="dd-align-right">4</td>
<td>The cohort table contains records identifying the subject(s) for defined cohort, during each period where they fit the cohort definition(s) defined in the cohort_definition table. Cohorts typically include patients diagnosed with a specific condition, patients exposed to a particular drug, but can also be Providers who have performed a specific Procedure. The subject of a cohort can have multiple, discrete records in the cohort table per cohort_definition_id, subject_id, and non-overlapping time periods. The definition of the cohort is contained within the COHORT_DEFINITION table. This table is not currently populated in STARR OMOP.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="dd-mono"><a href="#cohort_definition">COHORT_DEFINITION</a></td>
<td>Core CDM</td>
<td class="dd-align-right">7</td>
<td>Cohorts are a set of subjects that satisfy a given combination of inclusion criteria for a duration of time. The COHORT_DEFINITION table provides a standardized structure for maintaining the rules governing the inclusion of a subject into a cohort, and can store operational programming code to instantiate the cohort within the OMOP Common Data Model. This table is not currently populated in STARR OMOP.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="dd-mono"><a href="#concept">CONCEPT</a></td>
<td>Core CDM</td>
<td class="dd-align-right">10</td>
<td>The primary purpose of the CONCEPT table is to provide a standardized representation of medical Concepts, allowing for consistent querying and analysis across the healthcare databases. Users can join the CONCEPT table with other tables in the CDM to enrich clinical data with standardized Concept information or use the CONCEPT table as a reference for mapping clinical data from source terminologies to Standard Concepts. Each concept is uniquely identified by a concept_id and has a concept_name, which describes the concept. Concepts can be classified into different domains, such as drug, procedure, condition, etc., and can have relationships with other concepts.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="dd-mono"><a href="#concept_ancestor">CONCEPT_ANCESTOR</a></td>
<td>Core CDM</td>
<td class="dd-align-right">4</td>
<td>The CONCEPT_ANCESTOR table is designed to simplify observational analysis by providing the complete hierarchical relationships between Concepts. Only direct parent-child relationships between Concepts are stored in the CONCEPT_RELATIONSHIP table. To determine higher-level ancestry connections, all individual direct relationships would have to be navigated at analysis time. The CONCEPT_ANCESTOR table includes records for all parent-child relationships, as well as grandparent-grandchild relationships and those of any other level of lineage for Standard or Classification concepts. Using the CONCEPT_ANCESTOR table allows for querying for all descendants of a hierarchical concept, and the other way around. For example, drug ingredients and drug products, beneath them in the hierarchy, are all descendants of a drug class ancestor. This table is entirely derived from the CONCEPT, CONCEPT_RELATIONSHIP, and RELATIONSHIP tables.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="dd-mono"><a href="#concept_class">CONCEPT_CLASS</a></td>
<td>Core CDM</td>
<td class="dd-align-right">3</td>
<td>The CONCEPT_CLASS table includes semantic categories that reference the source structure of each Vocabulary. Concept Classes represent so-called horizontal (e.g. MedDRA, RxNorm) or vertical levels (e.g. SNOMED) of the vocabulary structure. Vocabularies without any Concept Classes, such as HCPCS, use the vocabulary_id as the Concept Class. This reference table is populated with a single record for each Concept Class, which includes a Concept Class ID and a fully specified Concept Class name.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="dd-mono"><a href="#concept_relationship">CONCEPT_RELATIONSHIP</a></td>
<td>Core CDM</td>
<td class="dd-align-right">6</td>
<td>The CONCEPT_RELATIONSHIP table contains records that define relationships between any two Concepts and the nature or type of the relationship. This table captures various types of relationships, including hierarchical, associative, and other semantic connections, enabling comprehensive analysis and interpretation of clinical concepts. Each relationship type is defined in the RELATIONSHIP table.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="dd-mono"><a href="#concept_synonym">CONCEPT_SYNONYM</a></td>
<td>Core CDM</td>
<td class="dd-align-right">3</td>
<td>The CONCEPT_SYNONYM table captures alternative terms, synonyms, and translations of Concept Name into various languages linked to specific concepts, providing researchers with a comprehensive view of how Concepts may be expressed or referenced. Researchers can leverage the CONCEPT_SYNONYM table to expand search capabilities and improve query accuracy by incorporating synonymous terms into data analysis and retrieval processes. Also, researchers can enhance their mapping efforts between local terminologies and standardized concepts by identifying synonymous terms associated with concepts in the CONCEPT_SYNONYM table.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="dd-mono"><a href="#condition_era">CONDITION_ERA</a></td>
<td>Core CDM</td>
<td class="dd-align-right">6</td>
<td></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="dd-mono"><a href="#condition_occurrence">CONDITION_OCCURRENCE</a></td>
<td>Core CDM</td>
<td class="dd-align-right">16</td>
<td></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="dd-mono"><a href="#cost">COST</a></td>
<td>Core CDM</td>
<td class="dd-align-right">22</td>
<td>The cost table captures the various financial aspects of healthcare events. It includes the cost of procedures, drug exposures, visits, and other healthcare events, and can capture charges, payments, and adjustments for these events. This table is not currently populated in STARR OMOP.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="dd-mono"><a href="#death">DEATH</a></td>
<td>Core CDM</td>
<td class="dd-align-right">7</td>
<td>OMOP CDM v5.4 DEATH table. Stores information about a Person&#x27;s death, including the date/time, cause, and source type. In STARR-OMOP, the cause of death fields are not currently available from source systems and remain NULL. This table contains only EHR-sourced (Epic) death records. External death records (CDPH, LADMF, DMF, etc.) are stored in the `_external_death_records` extension table, one row per external death record per person.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="dd-mono"><a href="#device_exposure">DEVICE_EXPOSURE</a></td>
<td>Core CDM</td>
<td class="dd-align-right">19</td>
<td>The Device domain captures information about a persons exposure to a foreign physical object or instrument which is used for diagnostic or therapeutic purposes through a mechanism beyond chemical action. Devices include implantable objects (e.g. pacemakers, stents, artificial joints), medical equipment and supplies (e.g. bandages, crutches, syringes), other instruments used in medical procedures (e.g. sutures, defibrillators) and material used in clinical care (e.g. adhesives, body material, dental material, surgical material). The distinction between Devices or supplies and Procedures are sometimes blurry, but the former are physical objects while the latter are actions, often to apply a Device or supply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="dd-mono"><a href="#domain">DOMAIN</a></td>
<td>Core CDM</td>
<td class="dd-align-right">3</td>
<td>The DOMAIN table includes a list of OMOP-defined Domains to which the Concepts of the Standardized Vocabularies can belong. A Domain represents a clinical definition whereby we assign matching Concepts for the standardized fields in the CDM tables. For example, the Condition Domain contains Concepts that describe a patient condition, and these Concepts can only be used in the condition_concept_id field of the CONDITION_OCCURRENCE and CONDITION_ERA tables. This reference table is populated with a single record for each Domain, including a Domain ID and a descriptive name for every Domain.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="dd-mono"><a href="#dose_era">DOSE_ERA</a></td>
<td>Core CDM</td>
<td class="dd-align-right">7</td>
<td>The dose_era table captures the time periods (eras) during which a person is exposed to a particular dose of a drug. A Dose Era is defined as a span of time when the Person is assumed to be exposed to a constant dose of a specific active ingredient. This table is not currently populated in STARR OMOP.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="dd-mono"><a href="#drug_era">DRUG_ERA</a></td>
<td>Core CDM</td>
<td class="dd-align-right">7</td>
<td>A Drug Era is defined as a span of time when the Person is assumed to be exposed to a particular active ingredient. A Drug Era is not the same as a Drug Exposure: Exposures are individual records corresponding to the source when Drug was delivered to the Person, while successive periods of Drug Exposures are combined under certain rules to produce continuous Drug Eras. Every record in the DRUG_EXPOSURE table should be part of a drug era based on the dates of exposure.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="dd-mono"><a href="#drug_exposure">DRUG_EXPOSURE</a></td>
<td>Core CDM</td>
<td class="dd-align-right">23</td>
<td>The DRUG_EXPOSURE table captures records about the exposure to a Drug ingested or otherwise introduced into the body. A Drug is a biochemical substance formulated in such a way that when administered to a Person it will exert a certain biochemical effect on the metabolism. Drugs include prescription and over-the-counter medicines, vaccines, and large-molecule biologic therapies. Radiological devices ingested or applied locally do not count as Drugs. This table contains one record per exposure, preferentially bringing in administration records, then dispense records then order records.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="dd-mono"><a href="#drug_strength">DRUG_STRENGTH</a></td>
<td>Core CDM</td>
<td class="dd-align-right">12</td>
<td>The DRUG_STRENGTH table contains structured content about the amount or concentration and associated units of a specific ingredient contained within a particular drug product. This table is supplemental information to support standardized analysis of drug utilization.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="dd-mono"><a href="#episode">EPISODE</a></td>
<td>Core CDM</td>
<td class="dd-align-right">13</td>
<td>The episode table captures aggregated information about periods of continuous engagement with healthcare or health maintenance activities. An episode is intended to represent a meaningful period of time within a broader context, such as a hospital stay, a period of illness, or a treatment cycle. The EPISODE table aggregates lower-level clinical events (VISIT_OCCURRENCE, DRUG_EXPOSURE, PROCEDURE_OCCURRENCE, DEVICE_EXPOSURE) into a higher-level abstraction representing clinically and analytically relevant disease phases, outcomes and treatments. The EPISODE_EVENT table connects qualifying clinical events (VISIT_OCCURRENCE, DRUG_EXPOSURE, PROCEDURE_OCCURRENCE, DEVICE_EXPOSURE) to the appropriate EPISODE entry. For example, cancers including their development over time, their treatment, and final resolution. In STARR-OMOP, the EPISODE table is currently populated only with episodes representing treatment plans (primarily for cancer patients). The EPISODE_EVENT table is currently not populated in STARR-OMOP.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="dd-mono"><a href="#episode_event">EPISODE_EVENT</a></td>
<td>Core CDM</td>
<td class="dd-align-right">3</td>
<td>The episode_event table captures the events that are part of an episode. It includes various types of healthcare-related events such as condition occurrences, drug exposures, or procedures that occur as part of a single episode of care. The EPISODE_EVENT table connects qualifying clinical events (such as CONDITION_OCCURRENCE, DRUG_EXPOSURE, PROCEDURE_OCCURRENCE, MEASUREMENT) to the appropriate EPISODE entry. For example, linking the precise location of the metastasis (cancer modifier in MEASUREMENT) to the disease episode. This connecting table is used instead of the FACT_RELATIONSHIP table for linking low-level events to abstracted Episodes. This table is not currently populated in STARR OMOP.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="dd-mono"><a href="#fact_relationship">FACT_RELATIONSHIP</a></td>
<td>Core CDM</td>
<td class="dd-align-right">5</td>
<td>The FACT_RELATIONSHIP table contains records about the relationships between facts stored as records in any table of the CDM. Relationships can be defined between facts from the same domain, or different domains. Currently, this table contains relationships between systolic and diastolic blood pressures taken from the same patient encounter record, as well as mother-baby relationships for babies delivered at Stanford. Relationships are always present in both directions, so there are two rows for any given fact pairing.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="dd-mono"><a href="#image_occurrence">IMAGE_OCCURRENCE</a></td>
<td>Core CDM</td>
<td class="dd-align-right">17</td>
<td>A record of image occurrences from the Vendor Neutral Archive (VNA). This does not include Echocardiograms, Ophthalmology images, or Pathology slides at present. We are also only including image occurrences that can be linked to the clarity procedure order information.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="dd-mono"><a href="#location">LOCATION</a></td>
<td>Core CDM</td>
<td class="dd-align-right">13</td>
<td>The location table represents a generic way to capture physical location or address information of Persons and Care Sites.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="dd-mono"><a href="#measurement">MEASUREMENT</a></td>
<td>Core CDM</td>
<td class="dd-align-right">23</td>
<td>The MEASUREMENT table contains records of Measurements, i.e. structured values (numerical or categorical) obtained through systematic and standardized examination or testing of a Person or Person’s sample.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="dd-mono"><a href="#metadata">METADATA</a></td>
<td>Core CDM</td>
<td class="dd-align-right">9</td>
<td>The metadata table metadata information about a dataset that has been transformed to the OMOP Common Data Model. At the moment for STARR OMOP, this table only contains a single entry specifying the OMOP CDM version (in this case, OMOP CDM version 5.4.2).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="dd-mono"><a href="#note">NOTE</a></td>
<td>Core CDM</td>
<td class="dd-align-right">17</td>
<td>The NOTE table captures unstructured information that was recorded by a provider about a patient in free text notes on a given date.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="dd-mono"><a href="#note_nlp">NOTE_NLP</a></td>
<td>Core CDM</td>
<td class="dd-align-right">14</td>
<td>The note_nlp table encodes all output of NLP on clinical notes. Each row represents a single extracted term from a note.The note_nlp table captures the detailed outputs of natural language processing (NLP) applied to the unstructured text found in the note table. This table contains the detailed annotations, the corresponding note identifiers, and the concepts identified through the NLP pipeline. This table is not currently populated in STARR OMOP.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="dd-mono"><a href="#observation">OBSERVATION</a></td>
<td>Core CDM</td>
<td class="dd-align-right">21</td>
<td>This table contains records of various observations made about individuals. It includes social history factors, ethnicity background, pregnancy and delivery observations, and other observations that are not captured in other tables.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="dd-mono"><a href="#observation_period">OBSERVATION_PERIOD</a></td>
<td>Core CDM</td>
<td class="dd-align-right">5</td>
<td>The observation period table is intended to contain records of spans of time in which a patient&#x27;s clinical event history is considered observable, i.e. clinical events that happen to the person are recorded in the event tables, and absence of records indicate such events did not occur during this span of time. Please note that since STARR-OMOP only contains records of clinical events that are present in the Stanford EHR systems, it is not possible to determine if the absence of an event means that the event did not occur or if the patient was instead treated in a different healthcare system.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="dd-mono"><a href="#payer_plan_period">PAYER_PLAN_PERIOD</a></td>
<td>Core CDM</td>
<td class="dd-align-right">17</td>
<td>This table contains information about the period of time that a Person is continuously enrolled under a specific health Plan benefit structure from a given Payer. Each Person receiving healthcare is typically covered by a health benefit plan, which fully/partially pays for (or directly provides) the care (billable healthcare services). These benefit plans are provided by payers, such as health insurances or state or government agencies. In each plan the details of the health benefits are defined for the Person or her family, and the health benefit Plan might change over time with increasing utilization (reaching certain cost thresholds such as deductibles), plan availability and purchasing choices of the Person. The unique combinations of Payer organizations, health benefit Plans and time periods in which they are valid for a Person (Payer Plan Periods) are recorded in this table.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="dd-mono"><a href="#person">PERSON</a></td>
<td>Core CDM</td>
<td class="dd-align-right">18</td>
<td>This table serves as the central identity management for all Persons in the database. It contains records that uniquely identify each person or patient, and some demographic information. If the patient is present in both SHC and LPCH Clarity, the SHC patient record is used.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="dd-mono"><a href="#procedure_occurrence">PROCEDURE_OCCURRENCE</a></td>
<td>Core CDM</td>
<td class="dd-align-right">16</td>
<td>The PROCEDURE_OCCURRENCE table contains records of procedures that have been performed on patients. The procedures are typically performed by healthcare providers and are recorded in the source data. For STARR-OMOP this includes ordered procedures and billed procedures.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="dd-mono"><a href="#provider">PROVIDER</a></td>
<td>Core CDM</td>
<td class="dd-align-right">13</td>
<td>The PROVIDER table contains a list of uniquely identified healthcare providers. These are individuals providing hands-on healthcare to patients, such as physicians, nurses, midwives, physical therapists etc.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="dd-mono"><a href="#relationship">RELATIONSHIP</a></td>
<td>Core CDM</td>
<td class="dd-align-right">6</td>
<td>The RELATIONSHIP table provides a reference list of all types of relationships that can be used to associate any two Concepts in the CONCEPT_RELATIONSHIP table, the respective reverse relationships, and their hierarchical characteristics. Note that Concepts representing relationships between the clinical facts in the FACT_RELATIONSHIP table are stored in the CONCEPT table and belong to the Relationship Domain.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="dd-mono"><a href="#source_to_concept_map">SOURCE_TO_CONCEPT_MAP</a></td>
<td>Core CDM</td>
<td class="dd-align-right">9</td>
<td>The SOURCE_TO_CONCEPT_MAP table is a legacy data structure within the OMOP Common Data Model, recommended for use in ETL processes to maintain local source codes which are not available as Concepts in the Standardized Vocabularies, and to establish mappings for each source code into a Standard Concept. STARR builds this table as an empty placeholder so that the OMOP 5.4 schema is complete; local source-code mappings are carried in the custom vocabulary instead.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="dd-mono"><a href="#specimen">SPECIMEN</a></td>
<td>Core CDM</td>
<td class="dd-align-right">15</td>
<td>The specimen table captures data on biological samples, or specimens, from a person. A specimen record indicates characteristics, such as date/time, specimen type, specimen source, and anatomic site of origin, in which the specimen was collected. This table is not currently populated in STARR OMOP.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="dd-mono"><a href="#visit_detail">VISIT_DETAIL</a></td>
<td>Core CDM</td>
<td class="dd-align-right">19</td>
<td>The VISIT_DETAIL table is an optional table used to represents details of each record in the parent VISIT_OCCURRENCE table. A good example of this would be the movement between units in a hospital during an inpatient stay. For every record in the VISIT_OCCURRENCE table there may be 0 or more records in the VISIT_DETAIL table. The VISIT_DETAIL table is structurally very similar to VISIT_OCCURRENCE table and belongs to the visit domain.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="dd-mono"><a href="#visit_occurrence">VISIT_OCCURRENCE</a></td>
<td>Core CDM</td>
<td class="dd-align-right">17</td>
<td>This table contains Events where Persons engage with the healthcare system for a duration of time. They are often also called “Encounters”. Visits are defined by a configuration of circumstances under which they occur, such as (i) whether the patient comes to a healthcare institution, the other way around, or the interaction is remote, (ii) whether and what kind of trained medical staff is delivering the service during the Visit, and (iii) whether the Visit is transient or for a longer period involving a stay in bed.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="dd-mono"><a href="#vocabulary">VOCABULARY</a></td>
<td>Core CDM</td>
<td class="dd-align-right">5</td>
<td>The VOCABULARY table includes a list of the Vocabularies integrated from various sources or created de novo in OMOP CDM. This reference table contains a single record for each Vocabulary and includes a descriptive name and other associated attributes for the Vocabulary. The primary purpose of the VOCABULARY table is to provide explicit information about specific vocabulary versions and the references to the sources from which they are asserted. Users can identify the version of a particular vocabulary used in the database, enabling consistency and reproducibility in data analysis.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="dd-mono"><a href="#external_death_records">_EXTERNAL_DEATH_RECORDS</a></td>
<td>Stanford extension</td>
<td class="dd-align-right">5</td>
<td>Extension table storing one row per external death record per person. External sources include CDPH (California Decedent Registry), LADMF (Limited Access Death Master File), other Clarity external death report organizations, and DMF (Social Security Death Master File). This table complements the OMOP `death` table, which contains only EHR-sourced (Epic) death records. External death records are separated because they carry lower confidence than EHR-confirmed deaths and should not be given the same weight by researchers. Unlike the `death` table, Clarity-sourced external records are not subject to the OMOP observation period date filtering. DMF-sourced records are limited to deaths at least 3 years before the data cut date due to SSA release lag. This table is custom to STARR-OMOP and is not part of the standard OMOP CDM.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="dd-mono"><a href="#variant_occurrence">_VARIANT_OCCURRENCE</a></td>
<td>Stanford extension</td>
<td class="dd-align-right">28</td>
<td>The VARIANT_OCCURRENCE table contains information about genetic variants identified in patients through genomic testing. This table is custom to STARR-OMOP and is not part of the standard OMOP CDM. Currently, it only contains variants identified via the STANFORD ACTIONABLE MUTATION PANEL FOR SOLID TUMORS (STAMP) test. The data is sourced from the Epic Genomics Suite, which incorporated STAMP tests starting in August of 2025. STAMP tests performed prior to this date are not currently included in this table.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="dd-mono"><a href="#whole_slide_imaging">_WHOLE_SLIDE_IMAGING</a></td>
<td>Stanford extension</td>
<td class="dd-align-right">20</td>
<td>OMOP extension table for whole slide imaging data from pathology specimens. It contains both information from the PHI-scrubbed whole slide imaging files (svs or isyntac) and source clarity. This table only contains information for slide images we have in GCP buckets with OMOP EHR information.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
</div>

## CARE_SITE {#care_site}

The CARE_SITE table contains a list of uniquely identified institutional (physical or organizational) units where healthcare delivery is practiced (offices, wards, hospitals, clinics, etc.). For Stanford University, this includes a range of care sites from inpatient hospital facilities to outpatient clinics and specialized centers such as immunization and campus-specific health services.

6 fields.

<div class="dd-static">
<table id="dt-care_site" class="table table-sm table-striped table-hover data-dictionary-table dd-layout-fields" data-dd-table="CARE_SITE">
<thead>
<tr>
<th scope="col" data-dd-key="field" data-dd-mono="true" data-dd-identifier="true" data-dd-compact="true" data-dd-filter="input" data-dd-width="240">Field</th>
<th scope="col" data-dd-key="required" data-dd-title="Req" data-dd-groupable="true" data-dd-compact="true" data-dd-filter="list" data-dd-align="center" data-dd-width="80" data-dd-filter-values="[&quot;&quot;, &quot;Yes&quot;, &quot;No&quot;]">Required</th>
<th scope="col" data-dd-key="type" data-dd-mono="true" data-dd-groupable="true" data-dd-compact="true" data-dd-filter="list" data-dd-width="125">Type</th>
<th scope="col" data-dd-key="references" data-dd-mono="true" data-dd-filter="input" data-dd-links="table" data-dd-width="165">References</th>
<th scope="col" data-dd-key="description" data-dd-clamp="true" data-dd-filter="input" data-dd-min-width="320" data-dd-grow="5">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td class="dd-mono">care_site_id</td>
<td class="dd-align-center">Yes</td>
<td class="dd-mono">INT64</td>
<td class="dd-mono"></td>
<td>Unique identifier for each care site.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="dd-mono">care_site_name</td>
<td class="dd-align-center">No</td>
<td class="dd-mono">STRING</td>
<td class="dd-mono"></td>
<td>The name of the care site as it appears in the source data. This field is used to identify the specific name or title associated with the care site, formatted as &quot;Care Site Name | Department Specialty.&quot; Examples of typical entries include: - &quot;EHC PHARMACY | PHARMACY&quot; - &quot;INFUSION TREATMENT CENTER-SNHC | INFUSION&quot; - &quot;RADIATION THERAPY SPLTY | RADIATION ONCOLOGY&quot; This format combines the department name with its specialty.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="dd-mono">place_of_service_concept_id</td>
<td class="dd-align-center">No</td>
<td class="dd-mono">INT64</td>
<td class="dd-mono"></td>
<td>This field summarizes the typical type of care provided at the site. Examples include Inpatient Hospital (ID: 8717), which covers overnight facilities like Stanford Hospital; Skilled Nursing Facility (ID: 8863), providing rehabilitative and nursing care; Outpatient Hospital on Campus (ID: 8756), representing campus-based outpatient services; Mass Immunization Center (ID: 8858), for mass vaccination programs; Home (ID: 0), representing healthcare in a patient’s residence; and Office (ID: 0), which refers to office-based outpatient care like physician offices Typically, if a care site provides multiple levels of care, assign the `place_of_service_concept_id` that represents the primary or most frequent type of care. For example, if most visits to a care site are inpatient, the `place_of_service_concept_id` should represent &quot;Inpatient Hospital.&quot; The VISIT_OCCURRENCE table can further refine specific settings for individual visits.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="dd-mono">location_id</td>
<td class="dd-align-center">No</td>
<td class="dd-mono">INT64</td>
<td class="dd-mono"></td>
<td>The location_id from the LOCATION table representing the physical location of the care site. This ID connects to the LOCATION table to capture the exact address or physical space associated with the care site.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="dd-mono">care_site_source_value</td>
<td class="dd-align-center">No</td>
<td class="dd-mono">STRING</td>
<td class="dd-mono"></td>
<td>The identifier of the care site as it appears in the source data. For STARR-OMOP, this is the Epic Clarity department ID.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="dd-mono">place_of_service_source_value</td>
<td class="dd-align-center">No</td>
<td class="dd-mono">STRING</td>
<td class="dd-mono"></td>
<td>The source value representing the place of service of the care site as it appears in the original data. This value can reflect specific labels like &quot;Inpatient Hospital,&quot; &quot;Office,&quot; or &quot;On Campus - Outpatient Hospital&quot; that map to broader `place_of_service_concept_id` categories.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
</div>

## COHORT {#cohort}

The cohort table contains records identifying the subject(s) for defined cohort, during each period where they fit the cohort definition(s) defined in the cohort_definition table. Cohorts typically include patients diagnosed with a specific condition, patients exposed to a particular drug, but can also be Providers who have performed a specific Procedure. The subject of a cohort can have multiple, discrete records in the cohort table per cohort_definition_id, subject_id, and non-overlapping time periods. The definition of the cohort is contained within the COHORT_DEFINITION table. This table is not currently populated in STARR OMOP.

4 fields.

<th scope="col" data-dd-key="type" data-dd-mono="true" data-dd-groupable="true" data-dd-compact="true" data-dd-filter="list" data-dd-width="125">Type</th>

## COHORT_DEFINITION {#cohort_definition}

Cohorts are a set of subjects that satisfy a given combination of inclusion criteria for a duration of time. The COHORT_DEFINITION table provides a standardized structure for maintaining the rules governing the inclusion of a subject into a cohort, and can store operational programming code to instantiate the cohort within the OMOP Common Data Model. This table is not currently populated in STARR OMOP.

## CONCEPT {#concept}

The primary purpose of the CONCEPT table is to provide a standardized representation of medical Concepts, allowing for consistent querying and analysis across the healthcare databases. Users can join the CONCEPT table with other tables in the CDM to enrich clinical data with standardized Concept information or use the CONCEPT table as a reference for mapping clinical data from source terminologies to Standard Concepts. Each concept is uniquely identified by a concept_id and has a concept_name, which describes the concept. Concepts can be classified into different domains, such as drug, procedure, condition, etc., and can have relationships with other concepts.

## CONCEPT_ANCESTOR {#concept_ancestor}

The CONCEPT_ANCESTOR table is designed to simplify observational analysis by providing the complete hierarchical relationships between Concepts. Only direct parent-child relationships between Concepts are stored in the CONCEPT_RELATIONSHIP table. To determine higher-level ancestry connections, all individual direct relationships would have to be navigated at analysis time. The CONCEPT_ANCESTOR table includes records for all parent-child relationships, as well as grandparent-grandchild relationships and those of any other level of lineage for Standard or Classification concepts. Using the CONCEPT_ANCESTOR table allows for querying for all descendants of a hierarchical concept, and the other way around. For example, drug ingredients and drug products, beneath them in the hierarchy, are all descendants of a drug class ancestor. This table is entirely derived from the CONCEPT, CONCEPT_RELATIONSHIP, and RELATIONSHIP tables.

4 fields.

## CONCEPT_CLASS {#concept_class}

The CONCEPT_CLASS table includes semantic categories that reference the source structure of each Vocabulary. Concept Classes represent so-called horizontal (e.g. MedDRA, RxNorm) or vertical levels (e.g. SNOMED) of the vocabulary structure. Vocabularies without any Concept Classes, such as HCPCS, use the vocabulary_id as the Concept Class. This reference table is populated with a single record for each Concept Class, which includes a Concept Class ID and a fully specified Concept Class name.

## CONCEPT_RELATIONSHIP {#concept_relationship}

## CONCEPT_SYNONYM {#concept_synonym}

The CONCEPT_SYNONYM table captures alternative terms, synonyms, and translations of Concept Name into various languages linked to specific concepts, providing researchers with a comprehensive view of how Concepts may be expressed or referenced. Researchers can leverage the CONCEPT_SYNONYM table to expand search capabilities and improve query accuracy by incorporating synonymous terms into data analysis and retrieval processes. Also, researchers can enhance their mapping efforts between local terminologies and standardized concepts by identifying synonymous terms associated with concepts in the CONCEPT_SYNONYM table.

</tr>

## COST {#cost}

The cost table captures the various financial aspects of healthcare events. It includes the cost of procedures, drug exposures, visits, and other healthcare events, and can capture charges, payments, and adjustments for these events. This table is not currently populated in STARR OMOP.

## DEATH {#death}

OMOP CDM v5.4 DEATH table. Stores information about a Person's death, including the date/time, cause, and source type. In STARR-OMOP, the cause of death fields are not currently available from source systems and remain NULL. This table contains only EHR-sourced (Epic) death records. External death records (CDPH, LADMF, DMF, etc.) are stored in the `_external_death_records` extension table, one row per external death record per person.

## DEVICE_EXPOSURE {#device_exposure}

The Device domain captures information about a persons exposure to a foreign physical object or instrument which is used for diagnostic or therapeutic purposes through a mechanism beyond chemical action. Devices include implantable objects (e.g. pacemakers, stents, artificial joints), medical equipment and supplies (e.g. bandages, crutches, syringes), other instruments used in medical procedures (e.g. sutures, defibrillators) and material used in clinical care (e.g. adhesives, body material, dental material, surgical material). The distinction between Devices or supplies and Procedures are sometimes blurry, but the former are physical objects while the latter are actions, often to apply a Device or supply.

## DOMAIN {#domain}

The DOMAIN table includes a list of OMOP-defined Domains to which the Concepts of the Standardized Vocabularies can belong. A Domain represents a clinical definition whereby we assign matching Concepts for the standardized fields in the CDM tables. For example, the Condition Domain contains Concepts that describe a patient condition, and these Concepts can only be used in the condition_concept_id field of the CONDITION_OCCURRENCE and CONDITION_ERA tables. This reference table is populated with a single record for each Domain, including a Domain ID and a descriptive name for every Domain.

3 fields.

## DOSE_ERA {#dose_era}

The dose_era table captures the time periods (eras) during which a person is exposed to a particular dose of a drug. A Dose Era is defined as a span of time when the Person is assumed to be exposed to a constant dose of a specific active ingredient. This table is not currently populated in STARR OMOP.

## DRUG_ERA {#drug_era}

A Drug Era is defined as a span of time when the Person is assumed to be exposed to a particular active ingredient. A Drug Era is not the same as a Drug Exposure: Exposures are individual records corresponding to the source when Drug was delivered to the Person, while successive periods of Drug Exposures are combined under certain rules to produce continuous Drug Eras. Every record in the DRUG_EXPOSURE table should be part of a drug era based on the dates of exposure.

## DRUG_EXPOSURE {#drug_exposure}

The DRUG_EXPOSURE table captures records about the exposure to a Drug ingested or otherwise introduced into the body. A Drug is a biochemical substance formulated in such a way that when administered to a Person it will exert a certain biochemical effect on the metabolism. Drugs include prescription and over-the-counter medicines, vaccines, and large-molecule biologic therapies. Radiological devices ingested or applied locally do not count as Drugs. This table contains one record per exposure, preferentially bringing in administration records, then dispense records then order records.

## DRUG_STRENGTH {#drug_strength}

The DRUG_STRENGTH table contains structured content about the amount or concentration and associated units of a specific ingredient contained within a particular drug product. This table is supplemental information to support standardized analysis of drug utilization.

## EPISODE {#episode}

The episode table captures aggregated information about periods of continuous engagement with healthcare or health maintenance activities. An episode is intended to represent a meaningful period of time within a broader context, such as a hospital stay, a period of illness, or a treatment cycle. The EPISODE table aggregates lower-level clinical events (VISIT_OCCURRENCE, DRUG_EXPOSURE, PROCEDURE_OCCURRENCE, DEVICE_EXPOSURE) into a higher-level abstraction representing clinically and analytically relevant disease phases, outcomes and treatments. The EPISODE_EVENT table connects qualifying clinical events (VISIT_OCCURRENCE, DRUG_EXPOSURE, PROCEDURE_OCCURRENCE, DEVICE_EXPOSURE) to the appropriate EPISODE entry. For example, cancers including their development over time, their treatment, and final resolution. In STARR-OMOP, the EPISODE table is currently populated only with episodes representing treatment plans (primarily for cancer patients). The EPISODE_EVENT table is currently not populated in STARR-OMOP.

## EPISODE_EVENT {#episode_event}

The episode_event table captures the events that are part of an episode. It includes various types of healthcare-related events such as condition occurrences, drug exposures, or procedures that occur as part of a single episode of care. The EPISODE_EVENT table connects qualifying clinical events (such as CONDITION_OCCURRENCE, DRUG_EXPOSURE, PROCEDURE_OCCURRENCE, MEASUREMENT) to the appropriate EPISODE entry. For example, linking the precise location of the metastasis (cancer modifier in MEASUREMENT) to the disease episode. This connecting table is used instead of the FACT_RELATIONSHIP table for linking low-level events to abstracted Episodes. This table is not currently populated in STARR OMOP.

## FACT_RELATIONSHIP {#fact_relationship}

The FACT_RELATIONSHIP table contains records about the relationships between facts stored as records in any table of the CDM. Relationships can be defined between facts from the same domain, or different domains. Currently, this table contains relationships between systolic and diastolic blood pressures taken from the same patient encounter record, as well as mother-baby relationships for babies delivered at Stanford. Relationships are always present in both directions, so there are two rows for any given fact pairing.

</table>

## MEASUREMENT {#measurement}

The MEASUREMENT table contains records of Measurements, i.e. structured values (numerical or categorical) obtained through systematic and standardized examination or testing of a Person or Person’s sample.

23 fields.

<div class="dd-static">
<table id="dt-measurement" class="table table-sm table-striped table-hover data-dictionary-table dd-layout-fields" data-dd-table="MEASUREMENT">
<thead>
<tr>
<th scope="col" data-dd-key="field" data-dd-mono="true" data-dd-identifier="true" data-dd-compact="true" data-dd-filter="input" data-dd-width="240">Field</th>
<th scope="col" data-dd-key="required" data-dd-title="Req" data-dd-groupable="true" data-dd-compact="true" data-dd-filter="list" data-dd-align="center" data-dd-width="80" data-dd-filter-values="[&quot;&quot;, &quot;Yes&quot;, &quot;No&quot;]">Required</th>
<th scope="col" data-dd-key="type" data-dd-mono="true" data-dd-groupable="true" data-dd-compact="true" data-dd-filter="list" data-dd-width="125">Type</th>
<th scope="col" data-dd-key="references" data-dd-mono="true" data-dd-filter="input" data-dd-links="table" data-dd-width="165">References</th>
<th scope="col" data-dd-key="description" data-dd-clamp="true" data-dd-filter="input" data-dd-min-width="320" data-dd-grow="5">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td class="dd-mono">measurement_id</td>
<td class="dd-align-center">Yes</td>
<td class="dd-mono">INT64</td>
<td class="dd-mono"></td>
<td>The unique key given to a Measurement record for a Person. This is the primary key for this table.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="dd-mono">person_id</td>
<td class="dd-align-center">No</td>
<td class="dd-mono">INT64</td>
<td class="dd-mono"><a href="#person">PERSON</a></td>
<td>A foreign key identifier to the person in the person table who is the subject of the visit.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="dd-mono">measurement_concept_id</td>
<td class="dd-align-center">No</td>
<td class="dd-mono">INT64</td>
<td class="dd-mono"><a href="#concept">CONCEPT</a></td>
<td>This is the field recommended for primary use in analyses, and must be used for network studies. This is the standard concept mapped from the measurement_source value which represents a measurement</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="dd-mono">measurement_date</td>
<td class="dd-align-center">No</td>
<td class="dd-mono">DATE</td>
<td class="dd-mono"></td>
<td>The date of the measurement</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="dd-mono">measurement_datetime</td>
<td class="dd-align-center">No</td>
<td class="dd-mono">DATETIME</td>
<td class="dd-mono"></td>
<td>This is the datetime of the measurement. If time is not available the convention is to set the time to midnight (00:00:0000).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="dd-mono">measurement_time</td>
<td class="dd-align-center">No</td>
<td class="dd-mono">STRING</td>
<td class="dd-mono"></td>
<td>This is present for backwards compatibility and will be deprecated in an upcoming OMOP-CDM version. Is it set to NULL for STARR-OMOP</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="dd-mono">measurement_type_concept_id</td>
<td class="dd-align-center">No</td>
<td class="dd-mono">INT64</td>
<td class="dd-mono"><a href="#concept">CONCEPT</a></td>
<td>This field can be used to determine the provenance of the Measurement record, as in whether the measurement was from an EHR system, insurance claim, registry, or other sources. For STARR-OMOP, it is set to EHR record (concept_id=32817)</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="dd-mono">operator_concept_id</td>
<td class="dd-align-center">No</td>
<td class="dd-mono">INT64</td>
<td class="dd-mono"><a href="#concept">CONCEPT</a></td>
<td>Operators are &lt;, &lt;=, =, &gt;=, &gt; and these concepts belong to the &#x27;Meas Value Operator&#x27; domain. This is intended for measurments that are ranges and it is not expected to be populated for most measurements.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="dd-mono">value_as_number</td>
<td class="dd-align-center">No</td>
<td class="dd-mono">FLOAT64</td>
<td class="dd-mono"></td>
<td>This is the numerical value of the Result of the Measurement, if available. Note that measurements such as blood pressures will be split into their component parts i.e. one record for systolic, one record for diastolic. The relationship for the two records (systolic/diastolic) is captured in the FACT_RELATIONSHIP table.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="dd-mono">value_as_concept_id</td>
<td class="dd-align-center">No</td>
<td class="dd-mono">INT64</td>
<td class="dd-mono"><a href="#concept">CONCEPT</a></td>
<td>If the raw data gives a categorial result for measurements those values are captured and mapped to standard concepts in the [&#x27;Meas Value&#x27;](https://athena.ohdsi.org/search-terms/terms?domain=Meas+Value&amp;invalidReason=Valid&amp;standardConcept=Standard) domain. (e.g. &#x27;normal&#x27;, &#x27;abnormal&#x27;, &#x27;positive&#x27;, &#x27;negative&#x27;, &#x27;detected&#x27;, &#x27;not detected&#x27;, etc.)</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="dd-mono">unit_concept_id</td>
<td class="dd-align-center">No</td>
<td class="dd-mono">INT64</td>
<td class="dd-mono"><a href="#concept">CONCEPT</a></td>
<td>This concept represents the mapping of the UNIT_SOURCE_VALUE column. It is mapped to the [Unit](https://athena.ohdsi.org/search-terms/terms?domain=Unit&amp;invalidReason=Valid&amp;standardConcept=Standard) domain that best represents the unit as given in the source data</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="dd-mono">range_low</td>
<td class="dd-align-center">No</td>
<td class="dd-mono">FLOAT64</td>
<td class="dd-mono"></td>
<td>This represent the lower bound of the range of the value_as_number as presented in the source date. This data is not always available. Ranges have the same unit as the VALUE_AS_NUMBER. These ranges are provided by the source and will remain NULL if not given.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="dd-mono">range_high</td>
<td class="dd-align-center">No</td>
<td class="dd-mono">FLOAT64</td>
<td class="dd-mono"></td>
<td>This represent the upper bound of the range of the value_as_number as presented in the source date. This data is not always available. Ranges have the same unit as the VALUE_AS_NUMBER. These ranges are provided by the source and will remain NULL if not given.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="dd-mono">provider_id</td>
<td class="dd-align-center">No</td>
<td class="dd-mono">INT64</td>
<td class="dd-mono"><a href="#provider">PROVIDER</a></td>
<td>The provider associated with measurement record, e.g. the provider who ordered the test or the provider who recorded the result.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="dd-mono">visit_occurrence_id</td>
<td class="dd-align-center">No</td>
<td class="dd-mono">INT64</td>
<td class="dd-mono"><a href="#visit_occurrence">VISIT_OCCURRENCE</a></td>
<td>The encounter in which the Measurement occurred.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="dd-mono">visit_detail_id</td>
<td class="dd-align-center">No</td>
<td class="dd-mono">INT64</td>
<td class="dd-mono"><a href="#visit_detail">VISIT_DETAIL</a></td>
<td>The VISIT_DETAIL record during which the Measurement occurred. For example, if the Person was in the ICU at the time the VISIT_OCCURRENCE record would reflect the overall hospital stay and the VISIT_DETAIL record would reflect the ICU stay during the hospital visit.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="dd-mono">measurement_source_value</td>
<td class="dd-align-center">No</td>
<td class="dd-mono">STRING</td>
<td class="dd-mono"></td>
<td>This field contains the exact value from the source data that represents the measurement that occurred. TODO: Update with more information about the column used.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="dd-mono">measurement_source_concept_id</td>
<td class="dd-align-center">No</td>
<td class="dd-mono">INT64</td>
<td class="dd-mono"><a href="#concept">CONCEPT</a></td>
<td>This is the concept representing the MEASUREMENT_SOURCE_VALUE and may not necessarily be standard.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="dd-mono">unit_source_value</td>
<td class="dd-align-center">No</td>
<td class="dd-mono">STRING</td>
<td class="dd-mono"></td>
<td>This field contains the exact value from the source data that represents the unit of measurement used.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="dd-mono">unit_source_concept_id</td>
<td class="dd-align-center">No</td>
<td class="dd-mono">INT64</td>
<td class="dd-mono"><a href="#concept">CONCEPT</a></td>
<td>This is the concept representing the UNIT_SOURCE_VALUE and may not necessarily be standard.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="dd-mono">value_source_value</td>
<td class="dd-align-center">No</td>
<td class="dd-mono">STRING</td>
<td class="dd-mono"></td>
<td>This field houses the verbatim result value of the Measurement from the source data. This includes numbers (e.g. 5.6), text (e.g. &#x27;normal&#x27;), etc.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="dd-mono">measurement_event_id</td>
<td class="dd-align-center">No</td>
<td class="dd-mono">INT64</td>
<td class="dd-mono"></td>
<td>If the Measurement record is related to another record in the database, this field is the primary key of the linked record.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="dd-mono">meas_event_field_concept_id</td>
<td class="dd-align-center">No</td>
<td class="dd-mono">INT64</td>
<td class="dd-mono"><a href="#concept">CONCEPT</a></td>
<td>If the Measurement record is related to another record in the database, this field is the CONCEPT_ID that identifies which table the primary key of the linked record came from.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
</div>

## NOTE_NLP {#note_nlp}

The note_nlp table encodes all output of NLP on clinical notes. Each row represents a single extracted term from a note.The note_nlp table captures the detailed outputs of natural language processing (NLP) applied to the unstructured text found in the note table. This table contains the detailed annotations, the corresponding note identifiers, and the concepts identified through the NLP pipeline. This table is not currently populated in STARR OMOP.

<td class="dd-mono">STRING</td>

## OBSERVATION_PERIOD {#observation_period}

The observation period table is intended to contain records of spans of time in which a patient's clinical event history is considered observable, i.e. clinical events that happen to the person are recorded in the event tables, and absence of records indicate such events did not occur during this span of time. Please note that since STARR-OMOP only contains records of clinical events that are present in the Stanford EHR systems, it is not possible to determine if the absence of an event means that the event did not occur or if the patient was instead treated in a different healthcare system.

5 fields.

## PAYER_PLAN_PERIOD {#payer_plan_period}

This table contains information about the period of time that a Person is continuously enrolled under a specific health Plan benefit structure from a given Payer. Each Person receiving healthcare is typically covered by a health benefit plan, which fully/partially pays for (or directly provides) the care (billable healthcare services). These benefit plans are provided by payers, such as health insurances or state or government agencies. In each plan the details of the health benefits are defined for the Person or her family, and the health benefit Plan might change over time with increasing utilization (reaching certain cost thresholds such as deductibles), plan availability and purchasing choices of the Person. The unique combinations of Payer organizations, health benefit Plans and time periods in which they are valid for a Person (Payer Plan Periods) are recorded in this table.

<td class="dd-mono">INT64</td>
<td class="dd-mono"><a href="#concept">CONCEPT</a></td>
<td>A foreign key identifier to the standard concept_id in the concept table. Upon mapping payer_concept_id to the standard concept_id in the concept table, this field represents the entity that would reimburse billable services for any provider(s) administering care to the person in each payer_plan_period record. It contains the standard concept obtained after mapping the qrda_sop_code_c field from STARR Common shc_payors and lpch_payors tables to the concept_code field in the concept table. The concept domain is &#x27;Payer&#x27; and the vocabulary is &#x27;SOPT&#x27;.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="dd-mono">payer_source_value</td>
<td class="dd-align-center">No</td>
<td class="dd-mono">STRING</td>
<td class="dd-mono"></td>
<td>Payer information as it appears in the source data. The value is represented as an array containing the fin_class_name, qrda_sopt_code_c, and sop_code_name values from the STARR Common shc_payors and lpch_payors tables.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="dd-mono">payer_source_concept_id</td>
<td class="dd-align-center">No</td>
<td class="dd-mono">INT64</td>
<td class="dd-mono"><a href="#concept">CONCEPT</a></td>
<td>A foreign key identifier to the source concept_id in the concept table. This field represents the entity that would reimburse billable services for any provider(s) administering care to the person in each payer_plan_period record, as it appears in the source data. It contains the source concept obtained after mapping the qrda_sop_code_c field from STARR Common shc_payors and lpch_payors tables to the concept_code field in the concept table. The concept domain is &#x27;Payer&#x27; and the vocabulary is &#x27;SOPT&#x27;.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="dd-mono">plan_concept_id</td>
<td class="dd-align-center">No</td>
<td class="dd-mono">INT64</td>
<td class="dd-mono"><a href="#concept">CONCEPT</a></td>
<td>This field represents the specific health benefit plan that the person in each payer_plan_period record is enrolled in. This is not currently populated in STARR OMOP due to the need for custom mapping.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="dd-mono">plan_source_value</td>
<td class="dd-align-center">No</td>
<td class="dd-mono">STRING</td>
<td class="dd-mono"></td>
<td>This field represents the specific health benefit plan that the person in each payer_plan_period record is enrolled in, as detailed in the source data. The value is represented as an array containing the benefit_plan_id and benefit_plan_name values from the STARR Common shc_payors and lpch_payors tables.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="dd-mono">plan_source_concept_id</td>
<td class="dd-align-center">No</td>
<td class="dd-mono">INT64</td>
<td class="dd-mono"><a href="#concept">CONCEPT</a></td>
<td>This field represents the specific health benefit plan that the person in each payer_plan_period record is enrolled in, as mapped from the source data. This is not currenlty populated in STARR OMOP due to the need for custom mapping.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="dd-mono">sponsor_concept_id</td>
<td class="dd-align-center">No</td>
<td class="dd-mono">INT64</td>
<td class="dd-mono"><a href="#concept">CONCEPT</a></td>
<td>This field represents the sponsor who finances the plan detailed in each payer_plan_period record. This includes self-insured, small group health plan and large group health plan. We are not populating this in STARR OMOP currently.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="dd-mono">sponsor_source_value</td>
<td class="dd-align-center">No</td>
<td class="dd-mono">STRING</td>
<td class="dd-mono"></td>
<td>This is the plan sponsor as it appears in the source data. We are not populating this in STARR OMOP currently.</td>

<tr>
<td class="dd-mono">sponsor_source_concept_id</td>
<td class="dd-align-center">No</td>
<td class="dd-mono">INT64</td>
<td class="dd-mono"><a href="#concept">CONCEPT</a></td>

</tr>
<tr>
<td class="dd-mono">family_source_value</td>
<td class="dd-align-center">No</td>
<td class="dd-mono">STRING</td>
<td class="dd-mono"></td>
<td>The common identifier for all people (often a family) that covered by the same policy. We are not populating this in STARR OMOP currently.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="dd-mono">stop_reason_concept_id</td>
<td class="dd-align-center">No</td>
<td class="dd-mono">INT64</td>
<td class="dd-mono"><a href="#concept">CONCEPT</a></td>

<td class="dd-mono">stop_reason_source_value</td>
<td class="dd-align-center">No</td>
<td class="dd-mono">STRING</td>

<td class="dd-mono">stop_reason_source_concept_id</td>
<td class="dd-align-center">No</td>
<td class="dd-mono">INT64</td>
<td class="dd-mono"><a href="#concept">CONCEPT</a></td>
<td>This field represents the plan stop reason as mapped from the source data. We are not populating this in STARR OMOP currently.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>

## PERSON {#person}

This table serves as the central identity management for all Persons in the database. It contains records that uniquely identify each person or patient, and some demographic information. If the patient is present in both SHC and LPCH Clarity, the SHC patient record is used.

18 fields.

<td class="dd-mono">INT64</td>

<td class="dd-mono">STRING</td>

<td class="dd-mono">gender_source_concept_id</td>
<td class="dd-align-center">No</td>
<td class="dd-mono">INT64</td>
<td class="dd-mono"></td>
<td>Foreign key to the concept in the Concept table representing the patient&#x27;s sex as it appears in the source data. The naming of this field as &#x27;gender&#x27; is outdated; it should not be used to study the patient&#x27;s gender identity.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="dd-mono">race_source_value</td>

<td class="dd-mono">STRING</td>
<td class="dd-mono"></td>

## PROCEDURE_OCCURRENCE {#procedure_occurrence}

The PROCEDURE_OCCURRENCE table contains records of procedures that have been performed on patients. The procedures are typically performed by healthcare providers and are recorded in the source data. For STARR-OMOP this includes ordered procedures and billed procedures.

16 fields.

<div class="dd-static">
<table id="dt-procedure_occurrence" class="table table-sm table-striped table-hover data-dictionary-table dd-layout-fields" data-dd-table="PROCEDURE_OCCURRENCE">
<thead>
<tr>

<th scope="col" data-dd-key="type" data-dd-mono="true" data-dd-groupable="true" data-dd-compact="true" data-dd-filter="list" data-dd-width="125">Type</th>
<th scope="col" data-dd-key="references" data-dd-mono="true" data-dd-filter="input" data-dd-links="table" data-dd-width="165">References</th>
<th scope="col" data-dd-key="description" data-dd-clamp="true" data-dd-filter="input" data-dd-min-width="320" data-dd-grow="5">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td class="dd-mono">procedure_occurrence_id</td>
<td class="dd-align-center">Yes</td>
<td class="dd-mono">INT64</td>
<td class="dd-mono"></td>
<td>The unique key given to a procedure record for a person.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="dd-mono">person_id</td>
<td class="dd-align-center">No</td>
<td class="dd-mono">INT64</td>
<td class="dd-mono"><a href="#person">PERSON</a></td>
<td>The person_id of the person for whom the procedure is recorded. This can be used to join to the person table to find more information about the person</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="dd-mono">procedure_concept_id</td>
<td class="dd-align-center">No</td>
<td class="dd-mono">INT64</td>
<td class="dd-mono"><a href="#concept">CONCEPT</a></td>
<td>The PROCEDURE_CONCEPT_ID field is recommended for primary use in analyses, and must be used for network studies. This is the standard concept mapped from the source value which represents a procedure</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="dd-mono">procedure_date</td>
<td class="dd-align-center">No</td>
<td class="dd-mono">DATE</td>
<td class="dd-mono"></td>
<td>This is the date when the procedure was performed or ordered on the patient. This is the start date of the procedure.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="dd-mono">procedure_datetime</td>
<td class="dd-align-center">No</td>
<td class="dd-mono">DATETIME</td>
<td class="dd-mono"></td>
<td>This is the date and time where the procedure was performed / ordered on the patient.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="dd-mono">procedure_end_date</td>
<td class="dd-align-center">No</td>
<td class="dd-mono">DATE</td>
<td class="dd-mono"></td>
<td>This is the date where the procedure ended. If not available is set to the same as procedure_date.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="dd-mono">procedure_end_datetime</td>
<td class="dd-align-center">No</td>
<td class="dd-mono">DATETIME</td>
<td class="dd-mono"></td>
<td>This is the date and time where the procedure ended. If not available is set to the same as procedure_datetime.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="dd-mono">procedure_type_concept_id</td>
<td class="dd-align-center">No</td>
<td class="dd-mono">INT64</td>
<td class="dd-mono"><a href="#concept">CONCEPT</a></td>

<tr>
<td class="dd-mono">modifier_concept_id</td>
<td class="dd-align-center">No</td>
<td class="dd-mono">INT64</td>
<td class="dd-mono"><a href="#concept">CONCEPT</a></td>
<td>The modifiers are intended to give additional information about the procedure. In some cases up to 4 modifiers can be associated with a procedure in the source data. In this column we are selecting only the first modifier from the source data.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="dd-mono">quantity</td>
<td class="dd-align-center">No</td>
<td class="dd-mono">INT64</td>
<td class="dd-mono"></td>
<td>This is the quantity of the procedure performed. If not available is set to 1.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="dd-mono">provider_id</td>
<td class="dd-align-center">No</td>
<td class="dd-mono">INT64</td>
<td class="dd-mono"><a href="#provider">PROVIDER</a></td>
<td>The provider associated with the procedure record, e.g. the provider who ordered or performed the Procedure.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="dd-mono">visit_occurrence_id</td>
<td class="dd-align-center">No</td>
<td class="dd-mono">INT64</td>
<td class="dd-mono"><a href="#visit_occurrence">VISIT_OCCURRENCE</a></td>
<td>The visit during which the procedure occurred.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="dd-mono">visit_detail_id</td>
<td class="dd-align-center">No</td>
<td class="dd-mono">INT64</td>
<td class="dd-mono"><a href="#visit_detail">VISIT_DETAIL</a></td>
<td>The VISIT_DETAIL record during which the Procedure occurred. For example, if the Person was in the ICU at the time of the Procedure the VISIT_OCCURRENCE record would reflect the overall hospital stay and the VISIT_DETAIL record would reflect the ICU stay during the hospital visit. Currently it is not populated for this table</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="dd-mono">procedure_source_value</td>
<td class="dd-align-center">No</td>
<td class="dd-mono">STRING</td>
<td class="dd-mono"></td>
<td>this is the source value as it appears in the source data. Includes a JSON string with the provenance of the data that includes names and codes.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="dd-mono">procedure_source_concept_id</td>
<td class="dd-align-center">No</td>
<td class="dd-mono">INT64</td>
<td class="dd-mono"></td>
<td>This is the concept representing the procedure source value and may not necessarily be standard. This field is discouraged from use in analysis because it is not required to contain Standard Concepts that are used across the OHDSI community, and should only be used when Standard Concepts do not adequately represent the source detail for the Procedure necessary for a given analytic use case. Consider using PROCEDURE_CONCEPT_ID instead to enable standardized analytics that can be consistent across the network.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="dd-mono">modifier_source_value</td>
<td class="dd-align-center">No</td>
<td class="dd-mono">STRING</td>
<td class="dd-mono"></td>
<td>This field houses the four possible modifiers found in the source data. It is a JSON string with the values of the four possible modifiers</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
</div>

The PROVIDER table contains a list of uniquely identified healthcare providers. These are individuals providing hands-on healthcare to patients, such as physicians, nurses, midwives, physical therapists etc.

<td class="dd-mono">STRING</td>

## RELATIONSHIP {#relationship}

The RELATIONSHIP table provides a reference list of all types of relationships that can be used to associate any two Concepts in the CONCEPT_RELATIONSHIP table, the respective reverse relationships, and their hierarchical characteristics. Note that Concepts representing relationships between the clinical facts in the FACT_RELATIONSHIP table are stored in the CONCEPT table and belong to the Relationship Domain.

## SOURCE_TO_CONCEPT_MAP {#source_to_concept_map}

The SOURCE_TO_CONCEPT_MAP table is a legacy data structure within the OMOP Common Data Model, recommended for use in ETL processes to maintain local source codes which are not available as Concepts in the Standardized Vocabularies, and to establish mappings for each source code into a Standard Concept. STARR builds this table as an empty placeholder so that the OMOP 5.4 schema is complete; local source-code mappings are carried in the custom vocabulary instead.

9 fields.

## SPECIMEN {#specimen}

The specimen table captures data on biological samples, or specimens, from a person. A specimen record indicates characteristics, such as date/time, specimen type, specimen source, and anatomic site of origin, in which the specimen was collected. This table is not currently populated in STARR OMOP.

## VISIT_DETAIL {#visit_detail}

The VISIT_DETAIL table is an optional table used to represents details of each record in the parent VISIT_OCCURRENCE table. A good example of this would be the movement between units in a hospital during an inpatient stay. For every record in the VISIT_OCCURRENCE table there may be 0 or more records in the VISIT_DETAIL table. The VISIT_DETAIL table is structurally very similar to VISIT_OCCURRENCE table and belongs to the visit domain.

## VISIT_OCCURRENCE {#visit_occurrence}

This table contains Events where Persons engage with the healthcare system for a duration of time. They are often also called “Encounters”. Visits are defined by a configuration of circumstances under which they occur, such as (i) whether the patient comes to a healthcare institution, the other way around, or the interaction is remote, (ii) whether and what kind of trained medical staff is delivering the service during the Visit, and (iii) whether the Visit is transient or for a longer period involving a stay in bed.

## VOCABULARY {#vocabulary}

The VOCABULARY table includes a list of the Vocabularies integrated from various sources or created de novo in OMOP CDM. This reference table contains a single record for each Vocabulary and includes a descriptive name and other associated attributes for the Vocabulary. The primary purpose of the VOCABULARY table is to provide explicit information about specific vocabulary versions and the references to the sources from which they are asserted. Users can identify the version of a particular vocabulary used in the database, enabling consistency and reproducibility in data analysis.

5 fields.

## \_EXTERNAL_DEATH_RECORDS {#external_death_records}

*Stanford extension — not part of the standard OMOP CDM v5.4.*

Extension table storing one row per external death record per person. External sources include CDPH (California Decedent Registry), LADMF (Limited Access Death Master File), other Clarity external death report organizations, and DMF (Social Security Death Master File). This table complements the OMOP `death` table, which contains only EHR-sourced (Epic) death records. External death records are separated because they carry lower confidence than EHR-confirmed deaths and should not be given the same weight by researchers. Unlike the `death` table, Clarity-sourced external records are not subject to the OMOP observation period date filtering. DMF-sourced records are limited to deaths at least 3 years before the data cut date due to SSA release lag. This table is custom to STARR-OMOP and is not part of the standard OMOP CDM.

5 fields.

## \_VARIANT_OCCURRENCE {#variant_occurrence}

*Stanford extension — not part of the standard OMOP CDM v5.4.*

The VARIANT_OCCURRENCE table contains information about genetic variants identified in patients through genomic testing. This table is custom to STARR-OMOP and is not part of the standard OMOP CDM. Currently, it only contains variants identified via the STANFORD ACTIONABLE MUTATION PANEL FOR SOLID TUMORS (STAMP) test. The data is sourced from the Epic Genomics Suite, which incorporated STAMP tests starting in August of 2025. STAMP tests performed prior to this date are not currently included in this table.

<td class="dd-mono">STRING</td>
<td class="dd-mono"></td>

<tr>
<td class="dd-mono">stamp_pipeline_version</td>
<td class="dd-align-center">No</td>

<td class="dd-mono">specimen_type</td>
<td class="dd-align-center">No</td>
<td class="dd-mono">STRING</td>
<td class="dd-mono"></td>
<td>The specimen type associated with the order for the variant record, such as &#x27;Blood&#x27;, &#x27;Tissue/Bone - Biopsy&#x27;, &#x27;Existing Patient Material&#x27;, etc.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="dd-mono">specimen_source</td>
<td class="dd-align-center">No</td>
<td class="dd-mono">STRING</td>
<td class="dd-mono"></td>
<td>The specimen source associated with the order for the variant record, such as &#x27;Blood, from Venipuncture&#x27;, &#x27;Saliva&#x27;, &#x27;Liver&#x27;, etc.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
</div>

## \_WHOLE_SLIDE_IMAGING {#whole_slide_imaging}

*Stanford extension — not part of the standard OMOP CDM v5.4.*

OMOP extension table for whole slide imaging data from pathology specimens. It contains both information from the PHI-scrubbed whole slide imaging files (svs or isyntac) and source clarity. This table only contains information for slide images we have in GCP buckets with OMOP EHR information.
